ops.title: container_proc_state /proc scan must skip /proc/$$ (self-match false positive)
ops.body:
The hermes container image has no grep/pgrep, so `probes.container_proc_state` scans `/proc/[0-9]*/cmdline` in pure sh. The obvious recipe (spec'd as "verified working") is BROKEN — a self-match false positive:

    for f in /proc/[0-9]*/cmdline; do c=$(tr "\0" " " <"$f" 2>/dev/null); case "$c" in *"hermes gateway run"*) exit 0;; esac; done; exit 1

The scanning `sh -c` process's OWN /proc/$$/cmdline contains the needle verbatim (it is literally in the command), so the scan matches itself and returns rc 0 (agent "alive") even when the agent is dead. Verified live 2026-07-18: bogus needle → rc 0 (wrong).

FIX (shipped in yclaw/probes.py container_proc_state): skip the scanner's own pid —
    case "$f" in "/proc/$$/cmdline") continue;; esac
Verified live: real needle → PASS, bogus needle → FAIL, 3/3 each; the `$(tr ...)` command-substitution fork does not race (tr execs immediately; its cmdline lacks the needle).

Also verified: Apple `container exec` DOES propagate real exit codes (exit 7 → host rc 7) — NOT the tailscale-ssh always-0 behavior. So deciding proc liveness from rc is valid here, unlike over Tailscale SSH.
